scenario: LEXP.7.20: two bindings of different schemas bind different facts, so they are never equal. Two Readings, r1 and r2, then one Alarm x1, and one pump. `eq` (`Reading a, Alarm b where a == b`) never fires; `ne` (the same with `!=`) fires once per pair, `ne r1/x1` then `ne r2/x1`: both matches complete when x1 enters, and LDET.5.5 orders them by their first pattern's fact. Every fact's key is `id` and the Alarm's value differs from both Readings', so equal keys cannot explain a result either way. PATH PINNED: the join test, scanned, in libds `rete/eval.c` `val_eq_unordered` (the same fact is the same rete id, and ids are engine-wide) and Mercury `ds.eval` `compare_outcome` (the same fact id). A runtime that raises a TypeError on every pair of both rules logs nothing.
rules_ds:
schema Reading scope logical:
    id: String key

schema Alarm scope logical:
    id: String key

rule eq:
    Reading a
    Alarm b where a == b
->
    log info "eq {a.id}/{b.id}"

rule ne:
    Reading a
    Alarm b where a != b
->
    log info "ne {a.id}/{b.id}"
